title: Hardrock Hundred 2026 Course Description - Clockwise Direction
claims: The 2026 course description is for the clockwise direction.
The description says it is not intended to be used as a navigation tool.
Cataract Putnam Pass is at mile 7.2 and 12,600 ft; Porcupine Cataract Pass at 8.6 and 12,230 ft; Grant Swamp Pass at 14.9 and 12,920 ft; Oscar's Pass at 21.3 and 13,140 ft.

After Kroger's the route climbs toward Virginius Pass; for 2026 a detour follows a faint singletrack for about 400 metres, then about 0.4 mile down Sydney Basin Road before rejoining Governor Basin Road.
Oh! Point is at mile 53.3 and 12,910 ft; American Grouse Pass at 60.7 and 13,020 ft; Handies Peak at 63.5 and 14,048 ft.
Cataract Pole Pass is at mile 77.2 and 12,200 ft; Maggie/Pole Pass at 85.4 and 12,530 ft; Buffalo Boy Ridge at 88.0 and 13,214 ft; Green Mountain/Stony Pass Ridge at 89.5 and 12,980 ft.
Mineral Creek is the biggest water crossing on the course and is crossed with a fixed rope.
No crew, spectators or media are allowed at the Highway 550 crossing or the Mineral Creek crossing, by order of the Colorado State Patrol.
The first miles leave Silverton, follow the Rainbow Trail along and above Highway 550 for just under 2 miles, then descend to cross Highway 550.
KT has no crew and no drop bags; Chapman crews must park in Ophir and hike about 1.4 miles plus 0.3 mile to the aid station.
Kroger's Canteen is described as having very limited space.
Ouray is the low point of the Hardrock 100 at 7,680 ft, and pacers may start there in 2026.
Engineer and Pole Creek are backcountry aid stations whose supplies are packed in.
Maggie Gulch has no crewing; one pacer may hike up from the base of the road at CR-2 to exchange.
Some sections are faint or off-trail, and the route at the top of Buffalo Boy Ridge can vary from year to year with snow and cornices.
The description warns of falls on snow, scree, talus and cliffs, fast-moving water, wildlife, rock fall, altitude sickness, lightning, cold and heat.
The course description warns that marmots devour course markers and pull them into dens, elk trample them into mud, and markers have been vandalised, stolen or maliciously relocated.

From Telluride the route follows paved streets to the Cornet Creek Trail, climbs steeply through Liberty Bell Basin to Mendota Ridge, traverses a scree field and climbs a steep loose trail to Kroger’s Canteen.
After Kroger’s the route descends three steep pitches; the first usually has snow even in dry years and may have a fixed line, with rock fall risk above and below.
From Governor Basin the route follows Yankee Boy / Camp Bird Road downhill for several miles to the edge of Ouray.

The Ouray Bear Creek Trail enters a steep, narrow gorge; hazards include rock fall, huge vertical drops off the right side and difficult stream crossings after heavy rain, and runners should lean left.
The last 3 miles of the drive past Eureka to Grouse Gulch are on a rough, narrow and occasionally congested road; 4WD is strongly recommended.
The trail from Grouse Gulch becomes less distinct and more braided; American Basin likely has some snow even in dry years.
From Burrows the route follows Cinnamon Pass Road downhill for 3 miles to Cottonwood Creek Road / CR-35 and then 0.5 mile to Sherman.
The Cataract Gulch Trail becomes less distinct with wetlands and willows; many runners have got off course in the huge willow stands and wetlands near Pole Creek, where elk trample markers.
The Maggie Gulch aid station is at the end of a rough, narrow 4WD road with steep drops.
